affordance_in_statement: The interference energy is given by the formula E(x1, x2, x3) = x1^2 + 4x2^2 + 9x3^2 - 2x1x2 I1,2 - 6x2x3 I2,3 - 3x1x3 I1,3, and a triplet is critically flawed if there exists a nonzero choice of real coefficients for which E is exactly 0.
secondary_shortcut_name: enumerating only common neighbors of an input edge
removal_suggestion: Change the x1x3 coefficient from -3 to +6, yielding E = x1^2 + 4x2^2 + 9x3^2 - 2x1x2 I1,2 - 6x2x3 I2,3 + 6x1x3 I1,3. This preserves the supplied example outputs and the existence of valid triples, but makes additional non-triangular patterns critically flawed.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: For each a, it examines pairs of neighbors b and c, thereby searching only for triangles.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The exact-zero quadratic condition is tuned so that a triangle is critically flawed.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: It processes an edge (a,b) and searches for a common neighbor c, again restricting candidates to triangles.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The exact-zero quadratic condition is tuned so that a triangle is critically flawed.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: It explicitly computes adj[a] intersect adj[b] and tests only common neighbors c > b.

common_affordance: The specially chosen quadratic coefficients make a triplet critically flawed precisely when all three pairwise interference links are present, so the problem reduces to finding the lexicographically smallest graph triangle.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It enumerates all triples with itertools.combinations, requiring Θ(n^3) candidates; with n up to 2000 this is infeasible regardless of the sparse edge bound.

recommended_edit: Replace only the term -3x1x3 I1,3 with +6x1x3 I1,3 in the energy formula. The original triangle-only reduction then fails: non-triangular triples can also have a nonzero real coefficient vector with zero energy, while the given example outputs remain valid.
